analysis_df = df.dropna(subset=["Date"]).copy()

print("Original rows:", len(df))
print("Analysis rows:", len(analysis_df))
print("Removed because of missing date:", len(df) - len(analysis_df))

**Repeated Record Decision**

Repeated rows were not automatically removed because the dataset does not include a unique transaction identifier, so identical-looking records cannot be confirmed as duplicate errors.

| Issue | Observation | Current Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Missing Date | 11,239 records | Exclude from time-series analysis |
| Negative Demand | Negative values exist, meaning not documented | Run sensitivity analysis; final treatment is determined in Section 18 |
| Zero Demand | Valid zero-demand periods may be meaningful | Keep as valid observations |
| Repeated Records | Large number of identical-looking rows | Keep because they cannot be confirmed as duplicate errors |
| Partial Years | 2011 and 2017 have incomplete coverage | Use 2012–2016 for modeling and forecasting |

**Finalize Negative Demand Treatment**

The sensitivity analysis showed only a small difference in total demand across the treatment options. Since the meaning of negative demand is not documented, the original values were retained rather than removed or replaced.

# Use complete years only
modeling_df = analysis_df[
    (analysis_df["Date"] >= "2012-01-01") &
    (analysis_df["Date"] < "2017-01-01")
].copy()

# Negative demand treatment
# Options: "keep", "exclude", "clip_zero"
negative_policy = "keep"

if negative_policy == "exclude":
    modeling_df = modeling_df[
        modeling_df["Order_Demand_Numeric"] >= 0
    ].copy()

elif negative_policy == "clip_zero":
    modeling_df["Order_Demand_Numeric"] = (
        modeling_df["Order_Demand_Numeric"]
        .clip(lower=0)
    )

print("Negative policy:", negative_policy)
print("Modeling rows:", len(modeling_df))
print("Date range:", modeling_df["Date"].min(), "to", modeling_df["Date"].max())

weekly_source = modeling_df[
    (modeling_df["Date"] >= "2012-01-02") &
    (modeling_df["Date"] <= "2016-12-25")
].copy()

weekly_demand = (
    weekly_source
    .set_index("Date")["Order_Demand_Numeric"]
    .resample("W-SUN")
    .sum()
)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))

plt.plot(
    weekly_demand.index,
    weekly_demand.values
)

plt.title("Weekly Order Demand (2012–2016)")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Total Order Demand")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("Weekly observations:", len(weekly_demand))
print("Start:", weekly_demand.index.min())
print("End:", weekly_demand.index.max())

# Rebuild a consistent weekly dataset using complete weeks only
week4_source = modeling_df[
    (modeling_df["Date"] >= "2012-01-02") &
    (modeling_df["Date"] <= "2016-12-25")
].copy()

week4_weekly = (
    week4_source
    .set_index("Date")["Order_Demand_Numeric"]
    .resample("W-SUN")
    .sum()
)

print("Raw modeling records:", len(week4_source))
print("Weekly observations:", len(week4_weekly))
print("Weekly start:", week4_weekly.index.min())
print("Weekly end:", week4_weekly.index.max())

reduction_ratio = (
    1 - len(week4_weekly) / len(week4_source)
) * 100

print(
    "Reduction from raw records to weekly observations:",
    f"{reduction_ratio:.2f}%"
)

m5_ml[
    "change_1_week"
] = (
    m5_ml[
        "lag_1"
    ]
    -
    m5_ml[
        "lag_2"
    ]
)

m5_ml[
    "change_4_week"
] = (
    m5_ml[
        "lag_1"
    ]
    -
    m5_ml[
        "lag_4"
    ]
)

m5_ml[
    "month"
] = (
    m5_ml[
        "Week"
    ].dt.month
)

m5_ml[
    "quarter"
] = (
    m5_ml[
        "Week"
    ].dt.quarter
)

m5_ml[
    "week_of_year"
] = (
    m5_ml[
        "Week"
    ]
    .dt.isocalendar()
    .week
    .astype(int)
)

m5_store_dummies = pd.get_dummies(
    m5_ml[
        "Store"
    ],
    prefix="Store",
    dtype=int
)

m5_ml = pd.concat(
    [
        m5_ml,
        m5_store_dummies
    ],
    axis=1
)

m5_store_dummy_columns = (
    m5_store_dummies
    .columns
    .tolist()
)

m5_feature_columns = [
    "lag_1",
    "lag_2",
    "lag_4",
    "lag_8",
    "lag_13",
    "lag_26",
    "lag_52",
    "rolling_mean_4",
    "rolling_mean_8",
    "rolling_mean_13",
    "rolling_std_4",
    "rolling_std_8",
    "rolling_std_13",
    "change_1_week",
    "change_4_week",
    "month",
    "quarter",
    "week_of_year"
] + m5_store_dummy_columns

m5_ml_model = (
    m5_ml
    .dropna(
        subset=[
            "Demand"
        ]
        +
        m5_feature_columns
    )
    .copy()
)

print(
    "Usable observations:",
    len(
        m5_ml_model
    )
)

**Forecasting Horizon Note**

The M5 evaluation uses a rolling one-week-ahead setting, where previously observed demand is available for lag-based features.

The 52-week test period does not represent a single 52-week-ahead forecast.
